g.text: The Equipment Hub lists the devices, and the top bar colours only a failure
Goal
On Android, the Equipment Hub stops drawing four large tiles and becomes a list
with one row per device, like iOS already has. On both platforms the list groups
the trainer with the power and cadence it supplies, a tap on a row opens a
device picker or that device's details as a sheet, and signal strength is three
bars instead of a dBm number. The top bar draws all four equipment icons on
every screen, first run included, and only a failed connection is drawn in red.
The design is the ISS-0519 canvas (https://claude.ai/artifact/K1LPrFBG4Kn7ShhSuF
S3nP), approved by Edwin on 2026-09-28, and the state table in
DES-0002-WorkoutSelectionNavigationAndChrome § 2.
Why this is allowed during the Android feature freeze
This redesigns two surfaces that FEAT-0125-TheChromeReportsEveryBoundDeviceAndTh
eHubIsBehindIt built inside PHASE-025-NavigationStructure. That phase carries
the third named exception to the PHASE-019 freeze (Edwin, 2026-09-22), and the
phase is still active. So this feature sits under that exception rather than
asking for a new one. It adds no new capability a rider did not have: every
action in the new Hub exists today behind a long-press, a ⋮ menu or a dialog.
The one new reading is the connected device's signal strength.
The exception's three conditions apply unchanged
(PHASE-025-NavigationStructure.md, "Freeze exception"): Android and iOS land
together, the PARITYMATRIX rows for the Hub and the top bar are updated, and the
screen gallery is regenerated for every screen this changes.
Why a new feature and not FEAT-0125 reopened
FEAT-0125 is done, passed an independent review on 2026-09-23, and its
requirements REQ-0214 and REQ-0215 are implemented with evidence against the
code as it stands. Reopening it would turn that evidence into claims about code
that is about to change. A new feature keeps FEAT-0125's record true for the
shipped Hub and gives this redesign its own review.
Scope
In scope
• The Hub as a list on both platforms. A "YOUR BIKE" card holds the Smart
Trainer row with Power and Cadence as indented child rows joined by a connector
line, and a caption under it. A "YOU" card holds Heart Rate, with its own
caption. A LIVE READINGS strip shows power, cadence and heart rate.
• Row actions. A failed or disconnected row carries a Reconnect button, an empty

path.title: FEAT-0130's gate: what is still missing before it can be accepted

g.data-label: Requirements: 0 of 30. This part counts the acceptance criteria of the requirements this feature implements, each ticked with evidence. Still missing: REQ-0224: All four icons are drawn on every screen that carries the top bar, first run included, and tapping them opens the Equipment Hub. Symbols: Android `EquipmentIndicators` loses `if (!equipment.anyBound) return` (`EquipmentIndicators.kt:66`); iOS `EquipmentIndicatorsButton` loses `if equipment.anyBound` (`HubChrome.swift:112`).; REQ-0224: *(Amended 2026-09-30, see Amendments.)* Each icon follows the state table in DES-0002 § 2: connected in the bar's text colour, connecting in the app accent, set up but not connected in grey, not set up in a fainter grey, couldn't connect in red with a filled dot. Symbols: Android `linkTint` (`EquipmentIndicators.kt:124`); iOS `EquipmentLabels.tint` (`HubChrome.swift:189`) and `SlotIndicatorGlyph` (`HubChrome.swift:135`).; REQ-0224: No icon is green or amber, and no icon carries a hollow dot. Android `linkTint` no longer returns `TrainerGreen` or `ResAmber`; iOS `SlotIndicatorGlyph` draws its dot for `.error` only.; REQ-0224: *(Amended 2026-09-30, see Amendments.)* A not-set-up icon is legible against the bar at the same size as the others. Today Android draws it at 22 % alpha and iOS at 35 % opacity, which is close to invisible. The new value meets 3:1 contrast against the bar background in light and dark themes, measured and recorded.; and 26 more.

path.data-label: Requirements: REQ-0225 *(Amended 2026-09-30, see Amendments.)* Each row shows the device's name and state in scheme A: a connected device's icon tile is lit in the app accent and its status text is plain secondary grey; connecting is the accent with a spinner; set up but disconnected is grey; a failure is red text on a red-tinted tile; not set up is a dashed tile reading "Not set up". A child row with no device of its own reads "From the trainer" or "From the power source". (open) · not yet

path.data-label: Requirements: REQ-0227 The picker shows three bars per device and no dBm text. Today Android prints `"${device.rssi} dBm"` (`ScannerModal.kt:125`) and iOS prints `"\(device.rssi) dBm"` (`ScannerSheet.swift:44`). (open) · not yet
path.title: Requirements: REQ-0227 The picker shows three bars per device and no dBm text. Today Android prints `"${device.rssi} dBm"` (`ScannerModal.kt:125`) and iOS prints `"\(device.rssi) dBm"` (`ScannerSheet.swift:44`). (open) · not yet

path.data-label: Requirements: REQ-0227 The bars follow one threshold table on both platforms: 3 bars (Strong) at −65 dBm or stronger, 2 bars (Fair) below −65 down to −80, 1 bar (Weak) below −80. Symbols: Android `signalBarsFor(rssi)`, iOS `SignalStrength.bars(rssi:)`, each with a unit test at −65, −66, −80 and −81. (open) · not yet
path.title: Requirements: REQ-0227 The bars follow one threshold table on both platforms: 3 bars (Strong) at −65 dBm or stronger, 2 bars (Fair) below −65 down to −80, 1 bar (Weak) below −80. path.data-label: Requirements: REQ-0227 A device with no reading shows no bars rather than one. iOS reports 0 for a peripheral it retrieved rather than discovered (`BluetoothService.swift:548`, `:644`) and 127 when the value is unavailable; both mean "no reading". (open) · not yet
path.title: Requirements: REQ-0227 A device with no reading shows no bars rather than one. iOS reports 0 for a peripheral it retrieved rather than discovered (`BluetoothService.swift:548`, `:644`) and 127 when the value is unavailable; both mean "no reading". (open) · not yet

path.data-label: Requirements: REQ-0227 The details sheet reads the connected device's signal and shows the same bars, with no word beside them. Neither app reads it today: Android gains a `BluetoothGatt.readRemoteRssi()` call in `BluetoothManager`, iOS a `CBPeripheral.readRSSI()` call and `peripheral(_:didReadRSSI:error:)` in `BluetoothService`. (open) · not yet
path.title: Requirements: REQ-0227 The details sheet reads the connected device's signal and shows the same bars, with no word beside them. Neither app reads it today: Android gains a `BluetoothGatt.readRemoteRssi()` call in `BluetoothManager`, iOS a `CBPeripheral.readRSSI()` call and `peripheral(_:didReadRSSI:error:)` in `BluetoothService`. (open) · not yet

path.data-label: Requirements: REQ-0227 The details sheet reads the signal only while it is open, and never while a ride is running. The details sheet is not reachable during a running ride (REQ-0225), and the read must not delay or fail a trainer control write. (open) · not yet
path.title: Requirements: REQ-0227 The details sheet reads the signal only while it is open, and never while a ride is running. The details sheet is not reachable during a running ride (REQ-0225), and the read must not delay or fail a trainer control write. (open) · not yet

path.data-label: Requirements: The bars carry no visible word, and a screen reader reads the strength: the bars' accessibility label is "Strong signal", "Fair signal" or "Weak signal", and "No signal reading" when there is none. Edwin, 2026-09-28, approving REQ-0227: 'The bars should not carry a visible label as well but yes accessibility should be considered for this.' (open) · not yet

Today Android draws it at 22 % alpha and iOS at 35 % opacity, which is close to invisible. The new value meets 3:1 contrast against the bar background in light and dark themes, measured and recorded.; and 26 more.
